finding.claim: The ban endpoint swallows the 403 raised by require_admin. flask.abort(403) raises werkzeug HTTPException, a subclass of Exception. The `except Exception` block only logs a warning and then execution falls through to do_ban(uid). Any authenticated non-admin user can therefore ban arbitrary users. The unban endpoint at line 24 does not catch the exception, so it is correctly protected. The ban endpoint is the only one with the flaw.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid. The user's g.user.is_admin is falsy.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid), the privileged ban operation, at admin.py:20

trace.note: Public Flask route /admin/users/<uid>/ban, POST. uid is attacker-controlled.
require_admin(g.user) is called inside a try block.
require_admin calls abort(403) for non-admins, which raises an HTTPException.
The handler only logs a warning. It does not re-raise or return.
do_ban(uid) executes regardless of the authorization result.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin is the only guard, and it is neutralised by the broad except. The route has no decorator, before_request hook or other middleware in the file. The unban route at line 26 calls require_admin without a try/except, so it is not affected. The log line at 19 also writes the user's name, which is minor and not the main issue. g.user is never populated in this file, so it depends on external middleware. The bypass holds for any authenticated non-admin. If g.user is unset, the handler raises AttributeError inside the try, which is also caught, so unauthenticated requests may reach do_ban too. do_ban is currently a stub, but the route is the protected operation.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 for non-admins, but the call at admin.py:17 sits in a try whose `except Exception` (admin.py:18-19) only logs, so the guard is neutralised. No decorator or before_request hook exists in the file.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:16-20 the HTTPException from abort(403) (line 11) is caught by `except Exception` and only logged, so do_ban(uid) at line 20 runs for any non-admin whose g.user is set; unban (admin.py:26) is unguarded by try and is safe. Two details in the finding are slightly off. The abort call is at line 11, not line 9. The claim that unauthenticated requests "may reach" do_ban is wrong: if g.user is unset, the handler's own g.user.get at line 19 raises again, which gives a 500 before do_ban. That does not change the authenticated non-admin bypass.
